Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Pedro Sánchez comparecerá el 3 de septiembre en el Congreso para abordar la crisis en Ceuta
items.description: La Junta de Portavoces ha acordado este miércoles fijar la comparecencia del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, para abordar la gestión de la crisis en Ceuta el próximo jueves 3 de septiembre. La fecha ha sido decidida por los grupos de la Cámara en una reunión celebrada esta mañana después de que el propio Sánchez pidiera comparecer para ofrecer explicaciones por la entrada de unos 80.000 inmigrantes el pasado 30 de julio en la ciudad autónoma. La Diputación Permanente iba a debatir también a partir de las 12 la comparecencia urgente del presidente. Este miércoles el BOE ha publicado además el real decreto que declara la “situación de interés para la seguridad nacional” en Ceuta, con un mando único vigente hasta el 31 de diciembre, liderado por el ministro Ángel Víctor Torres, que ha respaldado la versión de Marlaska sobre los avisos del CNI. Por su parte, el presidente del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha exigido convocar la Comisión de Secretos Oficiales para que el CNI aclare las “versiones” del Gobierno, ante el “desbarajuste” entre Robles y Marlaska, y ha reprochado al Ejecutivo que “alguien miente”. Además, este miércoles la ministra de Migraciones, Elma Saiz, regresa a Ceuta para seguir los trabajos de ampliación de los recursos temporales de acogida, donde ya se ha reubicado a más de un millar de personas que permanecían acampadas en la playa de El Trampolín. items.title: Raheem Sterling charged over Lamborghini crash, nitrous oxide possession
items.description: Former England international Raheem Sterling is set to appear in court next month after being charged with dangerous driving, possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. Sterling, 31, was charged following a single-vehicle crash on the M3 in Hampshire in May. The former Manchester City and Chelsea winger crashed his Lamborghini into motorway barriers near the Minley Interchange on the southbound carriageway on May 28, 2026. He was arrested following the incident and later released on bail pending further investigation. A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesperson said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3. “Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen. “The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange [Hampshire], on 28 May, 2026. “No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported. Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.” Police had initially suspected Sterling of “driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs”, although that allegation is not among the charges he now faces. Following the crash in May, a source close to Sterling told BBC Sport there was “no proof” that drugs were present in his system. The source also said the footballer had endured “an extremely tough couple of years” and had been made to “feel worthless” and “forgotten about”. Sterling is currently without a club after leaving Feyenoord at the end of last season. He joined the Dutch club on a short-term deal in February after leaving Chelsea by mutual consent. Chelsea had signed Sterling from Manchester City for £47.5m in 2022 following his successful seven-year spell at the Etihad Stadium. During his time at City, Sterling won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and one FA Cup. He subsequently spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal before returning to Chelsea, where he was excluded from the first-team squad and trained separately in 2025. Sterling began his senior career at Liverpool and went on to win 82 England caps between 2012 and 2022. He represented the Three Lions at three World Cups and two European Championships. His court appearance at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court is scheduled for September 15. items.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday. Footage aired on television showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area. Outside the hospital, an AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility. Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit. Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged. In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation. “The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”. Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said. She added that six bodies have been handed over to the parents, adding that the remaining would be handed over soon. Speaking to Geo News , Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said that the infants in the ward were either in incubators or on oxygen. He said the incident occurred at 6:45am due to a “blast in the air conditioner” inside the ward. He said that the blast caused the fire, which was exacerbated due to the presence of the oxygen tanks. He confirmed that 14 infants had been killed, adding that law enforcement agencies were on the ground. ‘We ran for our lives’ Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing. “After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said. Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive. “I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.” He added, “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they were here to investigate. “To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.” Mehmood said the fire erupted at 6am, and rescue and authorities reached at 9am. “People were helping themselves.” A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms. “People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP . “Give me my child,” Javeria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital, where ambulances had gathered. “I want justice.” Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward. Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of two of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes. Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement. Federal health secretary removed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate the incident. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families. “Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying. “The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said. In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri. The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement. It too stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting, it said. The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.” According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation. State-run APP reported that Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan was also included in the committee. Further, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general, had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire. The members of the committee included the director general of the Capital Emergency Services, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of the Capital Development Authority’s Electrical and Mechanical wing, representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company. The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations. The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours. Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”. “In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident. Nation expresses grief President Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”. “Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said. Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident. “My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said. As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the loss of innocent lives was an unbearable tragedy for the entire nation and expressed heartfelt sympathy and solidarity with the bereaved families. He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said that the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital. “Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration. First Lady and MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari also expressed “profound grief and sorrow over the tragic loss of newborn babies” and conveyed her “deepest sympathies to the bereaved families”. “The loss of innocent newborn lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing,” a statement by the Presidency quoted her as saying. She called for a “thorough, swift and transparent investigation” into the incident. PML-N President Nawaz Sharif said he was “deeply grieved” to hear about the deaths. He urged the government to take strict action against those responsible and ensure measures were put in place to prevent such incidents in the future. Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected. He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents. “Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future. National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants. In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents. United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) called for an urgent review as it expressed grief over the incident. “Unicef is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of at least 14 newborn lives following a fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad today. “We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families and all those affected by this devastating incident,” it said in a statement. The UN agency added, “ Every newborn deserves a safe start to life, and every mother and child should be able to receive care in a safe, secure health facility. It called for the urgent review and strengthening of fire prevention and safety standards across health facilities. The British High Commission in Pakistan termed the incident “heartbreaking news”. “Our deepest condolences and thoughts are with the parents and families at this unimaginably difficult time,” it said. The French embassy shared the sentiment, describing the incident as “deeply distressing”. “Our hearts go out to the families who lost their newborn children in the tragic fire at Pims in Islamabad. Loss of innocent lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing. Embassy of France extends its deepest sympathies to bereaved families and everyone affected by this tragedy,” it said in its message on X. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident. “The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said. It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”. It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals. The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”. Additional input from AFP and Reuters

items.title: 2026 U20 WWC: Black Princesses beat Polish side in friendly game ahead of tournament
items.description: Ghana’s U-20 women’s football team picked up a big win in their first friendly game in Poland as part of their preparations for the World Cup. The Black Princesses defeated Polish league side Ślęza Wrocław 4-0 in a preparatory test behind doors on Tuesday afternoon. Jacqueline Ntoso opened the scoring for Charles Samspon’s side after 35 minutes to give her side the lead at halftime. After the recess, Priscilla Mensah got an opportunity to double the lead but fluffed her finish two minutes into the second half. Twenty minutes later, the forward ensured she made amends with a close-range finish after receiving a pass from midfielder Ruth Amponsah. Amponsah, after providing the second goal, turned scorer three minutes later to extend the Black Princesses’ lead in the game. Diana Amoako added her name to the scoresheet with a superb strike in the closing stages to wrap up the victory for Ghana, who continue to build confidence for the global tournament. The game was a good test for the team, which continues its training in Poland towards its eighth successive appearance at the U-20 Women’s World Cup. The Black Princesses will open their tournament campaign against Ecuador on September 6 before facing South Korea and France in their other group games.

items.title: «Dégâts sans précédent» : les frappes iraniennes infligent des milliards de dollars de dommages aux sites de renseignement américains au Moyen-Orient
items.description: Selon un reportage exclusif de NBC News publie ce 25 août, les frappes iraniennes ont inflige aux postes de renseignement et au materiel de surveillance des etats-Unis dans la region un niveau de destruction superieur a tout ce que les agences d'espionnage americaines avaient connu jusqu'ici. Des infrastructures de la CIA et d'autres services durement touchees Quatre sources informees citees par la chaîne americaine indiquent que les bâtiments et les equipements de collecte de renseignements par la CIA et d'autres agences ont ete endommages. Le montant des reparations ou du remplacement se chiffre en milliards de dollars. « L'ampleur de la destruction est decrite comme depassant tous les dommages subis precedemment par les agences de renseignement americaines », rapportent ces sources. NBC: "Iran has inflicted unprecedented damage to US facilities in the Middle East." According to NBC, Iranian missile strikes and drone attacks have caused damage to US intelligence outposts and surveillance equipment in the Middle East, exceeding the scale of any destruction… pic.twitter.com/jYxDHEfp91 — 𝕊𝕡𝕣𝕚𝕟𝕥𝕖𝕣 𝕻𝕣𝕖𝕤𝕤 (@SprinterPress) August 26, 2026 Parmi les sites mentionnes dans les comptes rendus figurent la station de la CIA a Riyad, touchee par des drones en mars, ainsi qu'une installation dans la province de Sulaymaniyah en Irak, frappee en debut de conflit. Des systemes de radar et d'autres materiels partages entre le Pentagone et les services de renseignement ont egalement ete atteints dans plusieurs pays de la region. Les tensions se sont intensifiees depuis les frappes conjointes americano-israeliennes contre l'Iran en fevrier 2026. Teheran a repondu par des attaques contre les interets americains heberges dans des pays allies a Washington . Plus de 2 000 frappes iraniennes de missiles, drones et aeriens ont vise au moins 20 sites gouvernementaux americains dans huit pays. Un memorandum d'entente signe a la mi-juin sous mediation pakistanaise visait a mettre fin aux hostilites. Les discussions ont toutefois echoue sur les termes de l'accord et la libre navigation dans le detroit d'Ormuz. Dans ce contexte, le vice-ministre des Affaires etrangeres, Gharibabadi, a mis en garde les etats-Unis contre toute nouvelle agression et menace d'utiliser des moyens militaires jusqu'alors non utilises. ⚠️ IRAN ESCALATES RHETORIC OVER NEW CAPABILITIES 🇮🇷 Deputy FM Gharibabadi warns the US against further aggression, threatening to unveil undisclosed military assets. Tensions spike amid volatile maritime activity near the STRAIT OF HORMUZ. 🚢📡 #IRAN #OSINT — OSN - Observer Security Network (@OSN_Reports) August 26, 2026 Le Congres doit desormais trouver des fonds pour restaurer les installations touchees, tandis que les responsables americains reevaluent le deploiement du personnel et des ressources de renseignement dans une zone exposee aux drones et missiles iraniens. Des experts, comme Seth Jones du Center for Strategic and International Studies , soulignent que la guerre a revele des lacunes dans la defense des bases americaines. items.title: ‘We don’t work with visa agents’ — German Embassy warns Nigerians
items.description: The German Embassy in Nigeria has warned visa applicants against relying on so-called “visa agents” for information about travelling to Germany. In a recent tweet, the embassy urged Nigerians to be cautious about information provided by individuals claiming to have special knowledge or access to the German visa process. The embassy said applicants should verify visa-related information directly with the German mission rather than relying on claims from visa agents. “Beware of misinformation. Save yourself the hassle & just ask us directly,” the embassy said. It also asked Nigerians to share some of the claims they had heard from “visa agents” in the comments, saying it would address them in upcoming posts. The German mission made its position on visa agents clear, stating: “We DO NOT WORK with any ‘Visa Agents’!” The embassy added that applicants do not need to depend on agents to access official information, as details about German visas and application procedures are freely available through its website. The warning comes as many Nigerians seeking to travel to Germany rely on third parties for assistance with visa applications, including tourism, study, employment and family reunification. The embassy’s clarification means applicants should be wary of anyone claiming to represent the German Embassy or suggesting that they have special influence over visa decisions. Official German visa information for applicants in Nigeria is available through the German Missions in Nigeria. Vanguard News The post ‘We don’t work with visa agents’ — German Embassy warns Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Référendum sur l’Europe : un poisson nommé Islande
items.description: Ce 29 août 2026, les Islandais sont appelés aux urnes pour un référendum sur la réouverture d’un processus d’adhésion à l’Union européenne (UE), interrompu depuis plus d’une décennie. Le scrutin est consultatif, même si le gouvernement s’est engagé à en respecter le résultat. Si le « oui » l’emporte, de nouvelles négociations seraient engagées et un accord final d’adhésion devrait ensuite être soumis aux Islandais. À quelques jours du vote, les sondages témoignent d’un pays profondément partagé, illustrant un dilemme de souveraineté et de puissance. Il s’agit aussi, en miroir, d’une potentielle réflexion stratégique à venir pour l’UE : est-elle capable de développer une nouvelle ambition maritime et halieutique si l’Islande intègre la Communauté ? Points de repère spatio-temporels Sur une carte, l’Islande semble périphérique, avec à peine moins d’un demi-million d’habitants sur cette île volcanique de l’Atlantique Nord. Mais sur une carte océanique, elle trouve davantage de centralité, avec une position charnière entre Europe, Amérique du Nord et Arctique. Tout le paradoxe géopolitique islandais est là : petite puissance terrestre et démographique, mais grande puissance maritime et halieutique. La Chine ne s’y trompe d’ailleurs pas, souhaitant placer des pions en Islande dans le cadre de sa stratégie des routes polaires de la soie. L’Islande est déjà profondément imbriquée dans l’espace européen. Membre fondateur de l’Organisation du traité de l’Atlantique Nord (OTAN) en 1949, elle appartient à l’Association européenne de libre-échange depuis 1970, à l’Espace économique européen (EEE) depuis 1994 et à l’espace Schengen depuis 2001. Elle applique ainsi une partie considérable des règles du marché intérieur européen et participe à de nombreux programmes sans être membre de l’UE. Son économie est également très connectée au continent. Cette proximité économique et institutionnelle rend parfois difficile à percevoir ce qui sépare encore véritablement Reykjavik de Bruxelles. Or, deux secteurs essentiels restent précisément à l’écart du fonctionnement ordinaire de l’EEE : l’agriculture et la pêche. Ce n’est évidemment pas anodin. L’une des singularités de l’Islande réside dans la place occupée par ses ressources naturelles et surtout marines. Sa prospérité, son histoire et une partie de son identité se sont construites autour de cette mer nourricière. L’Islande avait officiellement déposé sa candidature à l’UE en 2009, dans le contexte de la grave crise financière internationale, qui n’avait pas épargné le pays. Les négociations furent suspendues en 2013, avant que le processus ne soit abandonné en 2015. Parmi les principaux points de friction figurait déjà la pêche. Plus d’une décennie après, le contexte global a changé, avec notamment ces velléités trumpiennes sur le Groenland qui perturbent les raisonnements islandais et modifient les enjeux dans l’Arctique pour l’UE. Or, si l’Islande et l’UE peuvent trouver de nouvelles raisons géopolitiques à se rapprocher, la pêche reste l’épine dorsale des divisions. La singularité halieutique islandaise La pêche et l’aquaculture représentent environ 7 % du PIB, 5 % de l’emploi et près de 40 % des exportations islandaises de marchandises. Les captures atteignent en moyenne 1,4 million de tonnes par an, dont environ 710 000 tonnes d’espèces démersales – parmi lesquelles quelque 220 000 tonnes de morue – et 550 000 tonnes de poissons pélagiques comme le capelan, le maquereau ou le hareng. L’aquaculture progresse, notamment en saumon. Il faut dire que de nombreux pays de l’UE en raffolent (à commencer par la France) sans en produire sur leurs littoraux ou leurs sols. Parler d’une éventuelle adhésion de l’Islande à l’Union européenne sans parler de poisson reviendrait presque à parler de l’Arabie saoudite sans évoquer le pétrole. Car la pêche islandaise n’est pas une activité économique périphérique qu’il faudrait maintenir artificiellement en vie. Au contraire, les Islandais en sont fiers et misent sur ce secteur. Ce dernier s’avère créateur de richesses, exportateur, performant et fortement intégré aux circuits mondiaux. Sa ressource sauvage – cabillaud, églefin, espèces pélagiques notamment – comme sa production aquacole sont très recherchées sur des marchés où la concurrence est mondiale. Les produits islandais sont largement présents sur le marché européen. Les opérateurs se sont adaptés au Brexit, avec notamment un redéploiement d’une partie des flux vers les Pays-Bas avant redistribution vers d’autres États membres. L’Islande dispose donc déjà du débouché européen sans appartenir à l’UE. La pêche en Islande, attribut de souveraineté Entre les années 1950 et 1970, les fameuses « guerres de la morue » opposèrent l’Islande au Royaume-Uni autour de l’extension des zones de pêche islandaises. Reykjavik parvint progressivement à imposer son contrôle jusqu’à 200 milles nautiques de ses côtes. Pour cette micro-nation insulaire, la maîtrise de la mer et de ses ressources est ainsi devenue une manifestation particulièrement concrète de l’indépendance nationale. Cette mémoire demeure présente. Là où d’autres États pensent leur souveraineté d’abord à travers leurs frontières terrestres, l’Islande la pense aussi à travers ses poissons, ses quotas, ses navires et son espace maritime. Et c’est ici la tension majeure d’une éventuelle adhésion à l’UE : pour la pêche islandaise, l’intérêt à y entrer reste faible. Pour Reykjavik, la question est d’abord celle de la souveraineté. L’Islande détermine largement ses règles de gestion des ressources halieutiques et défend jalousement le contrôle de ses stocks, de ses quotas et de l’accès à ses eaux. Une éventuelle adhésion obligerait pourtant l’Islande à négocier son intégration à la politique commune de la pêche (PCP). Les modalités feraient évidemment l’objet de discussions, mais le principe est politiquement explosif : pourquoi transférer une partie de sa capacité de décision à Bruxelles sur une ressource considérée comme nationale, stratégique et particulièrement bien valorisée ? Pourquoi modifier un modèle qui fonctionne, accepter davantage de règles communes et renoncer à une partie d’autonomie alors que l’accès au marché européen existe déjà ? Si pour Bruxelles, la pêche pourrait constituer l’une des raisons de vouloir l’Islande dans l’Union, pour une partie du secteur halieutique islandais, elle constitue précisément l’une des meilleures raisons de rester dehors. Entrer dans l’UE en rejetant le poisson ? Soyons réalistes : la PCP ne fait pas rêver Reykjavik. Cette évaluation est d’autant plus légitime que la pêche européenne traverse elle-même de fortes tensions et que l’UE peine à définir un cap clair en matière de stratégie halieutique. Rappelons ici que les produits de la mer font partie des plus grandes dépendances alimentaires dans la majorité des pays de l’UE. Cela vaut pour la France, grande puissance bleue, sauf dans l’assiette. Depuis plusieurs décennies, la PCP cherche à concilier trois impératifs : exploiter économiquement les ressources, assurer le renouvellement des stocks et protéger les écosystèmes marins. Quotas, limitations de l’effort de pêche, contraintes pesant sur les capacités des flottes (coût de l’énergie, vieillissement des professionnels, etc.), développement des aires marines protégées et multiplication des normes environnementales alimentent chez une partie des pêcheurs européens le sentiment d’un espace halieutique qui se rétrécit. La flotte européenne diminue et sa vétuste inquiète. Certains armateurs connaissent de sérieuses difficultés économiques, d’autant que la compétition internationale s’est intensifiée. L’UE veut protéger ses zones maritimes, mais elle importe donc massivement les produits de la mer qu’elle consomme. Réduire la pression de pêche dans les eaux européennes peut produire un bénéfice environnemental local. Mais si la consommation demeure et si elle est satisfaite par davantage d’importations, la pression productive ne disparaît pas nécessairement. Elle peut aussi être déplacée vers d’autres mers. La question ne serait-elle pas de déterminer comment l’Europe peut simultanément préserver ses ressources et préserver sa capacité à produire ? Cela pourrait être le narratif islandais, d’autant que l’on voit mal ce pays ne pas rester une puissance halieutique quand bien même l’adhésion à l’UE se profilerait. Dit autrement, Reykjavik pourrait-elle faire évoluer la PCP et la vision halieutique de l’UE ? Se tourner vers l’avenir Le Brexit a rétréci l’Europe maritime, l’Islande pourrait l’agrandir. La sortie du Royaume-Uni en 2020 a accéléré les problématiques pour les pêcheries européennes. L’hypothèse d’une intégration de l’Islande dans l’UE pourrait rebattre les cartes, une décennie plus tard. La zone économique exclusive islandaise représente environ 758 000 km². Son adhésion accroîtrait donc considérablement l’espace maritime relevant d’un État membre de l’UE. Les captures islandaises représentent à elles seules l’équivalent d’environ 30 % des volumes actuellement pêchés par l’UE27. Avec l’Islande, l’UE réaliserait 5 % des captures mondiales. Aujourd’hui, l’Islande est simultanément partenaire et redoutable concurrent halieutique de l’Union européenne. Sa flotte est productive, son expertise scientifique reconnue, son industrie de transformation performante et son système de gestion des ressources fortement structuré. Avec la Norvège, elle illustre une forme de puissance halieutique nordique fondée sur l’association entre ressources, technologie, efficacité des flottes et gestion des stocks. Tant qu’elle reste extérieure à l’UE, cette puissance s’exerce en partie face à elle : compétition commerciale, négociations sur les stocks partagés, accès aux marchés, quotas et rapports de force autour des espèces migratoires. Mais l’adhésion changerait la perspective. L’Islande intégrée pourrait devenir une contributrice majeure à la capacité halieutique et alimentaire européenne. À une condition cependant : que l’UE souhaite redevenir une puissance halieutique et s’assume comme protagoniste sur les affaires maritimes de l’Arctique. C’est là que le référendum islandais devient un débat européen si le oui l’emporte le 28 août et si le processus d’adhésion s’en trouve relancé. L’UE transformera l’Islande, mais l’Islande pourrait aussi faire évoluer l’Europe halieutique. Il ne s’agirait évidemment pas de revenir sur la nécessité d’une gestion durable des ressources. Une puissance halieutique ne peut l’être durablement qu’en préservant le capital biologique sur lequel elle repose. Mais soutenabilité et puissance ne sont pas nécessairement contradictoires. Sous cet angle, un parallèle peut être esquissé avec l’Ukraine agricole, qui apporterait des forces considérables à l’UE dans ce secteur en cas d’adhésion de Kiev demain, si et seulement si une vision géopolitique et géoéconomique s’exprime. Sans cela, l’agriculture constituera le dossier le plus explosif et le plus fracturant du dialogue euro-ukrainien. Les situations sont évidemment très différentes par leur taille, leur histoire et leur contexte géopolitique. Mais elles interrogent toutes deux la manière dont l’Union envisage ses futurs élargissements Ukraine et Islande posent ainsi, chacune dans leur domaine, une même question à Bruxelles : l’élargissement consiste-t-il seulement à étendre un espace juridique et réglementaire, ou peut-il aussi servir à agréger de nouvelles capacités de puissance ? Quand les poissons déplacent la géopolitique Ajoutons une brique aux réflexions précédentes. La question euro-islandaise devient encore plus stratégique avec le changement climatique. Le réchauffement des eaux modifie progressivement la répartition géographique de certaines espèces. Les stocks évoluent, migrent ou deviennent plus variables. Certaines espèces apparaissent davantage dans certaines zones tandis qu’elles en délaissent d’autres. La géographie de la pêche n’est donc pas immuable. Les tensions observées autour du maquereau entre l’Islande, les îles Féroé, la Norvège et l’UE en fournissent une illustration. Elles pourraient préfigurer d’autres controverses à mesure que le changement climatique transforme les écosystèmes de l’Atlantique Nord. Un poisson qui change de latitude peut déplacer de la valeur économique, chambouler des quotas et durcir des discussions diplomatiques. La gouvernance halieutique devient ainsi une forme de géopolitique climatique. Elle oblige les États côtiers à négocier simultanément la conservation de ressources mobiles, l’accès aux zones de pêche et le partage de la richesse qu’elles génèrent. Cette évolution renforce mécaniquement la valeur stratégique des États disposant à la fois d’importants espaces maritimes, d’une expertise scientifique reconnue et d’une industrie halieutique performante. L’Islande réunit précisément ces trois caractéristiques. La mer pousse l’Islande à préserver son autonomie ; la géopolitique peut la pousser vers l’UE. Contrairement à la Norvège, l’Islande ne dispose pas de la même profondeur financière et énergétique pour absorber les chocs d’un environnement international plus incertain. Dans un monde où les rapports de force reviennent au premier plan, la petite taille démographique peut redevenir une vulnérabilité. La campagne référendaire conduit naturellement les Islandais à s’interroger sur ce que l’UE pourrait leur apporter : sécurité, influence politique, stabilité économique ou perspective d’intégration monétaire. La dynamique géopolitique en Arctique pousse au rapprochement avec l’UE. Mais la souveraineté halieutique les invite à la prudence. Mais il convient de poser aussi la question de ce que gagnerait l’UE avec l’Islande. Dans cette perspective, le sujet halieutique, avec ses composantes spatio-maritimes et économico-alimentaires, est inévitable. L’article Référendum sur l’Europe : un poisson nommé Islande est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Immersion patriotique obligatoire 2026 : La cérémonie de clôture prévue ce jeudi 27 août au Stade du 4-Août
items.description: La session 2026 de l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire dans la région du Kadiogo s'achève ce jeudi 27 août 2026. La cérémonie solennelle de clôture se tiendra à partir de 7 heures au Stade du 4-Août, sous le très haut patronage du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Après plusieurs jours d'immersion, les appelés de la région du Kadiogo retrouveront leurs familles à compter de ce mercredi 26 août à 17 h 30. Toutefois, ils devront à nouveau se présenter au stade du 4-Août dès 4 heures du matin le jeudi 27 août pour prendre part à la cérémonie officielle de clôture. Selon les dispositions communiquées par la Cellule régionale d'organisation de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire du Kadiogo (CRIPO/2026), chaque appelé devra obligatoirement se présenter dans la tenue exigée, à savoir le tee-shirt de l'appelé et un pantalon noir. La présence effective des participants à cette cérémonie est présentée comme une obligation. Les parents des appelés sont également invités à prendre part à cette cérémonie. Pour faciliter leur accès au stade, ils seront reçus aux portes numéros 2 et 19. Les organisateurs invitent par ailleurs l'ensemble des participants à respecter strictement les consignes de sécurité durant la cérémonie. A l'issue de la cérémonie, les parents devront raccompagner les appelés sur leurs sites respectifs. Cette étape permettra notamment aux participants d'entrer en possession de leurs attestations de participation à l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire. Lefaso.net

Route nationale 5 : Le poste de péage de Koubri change de place pour améliorer la fluidité du trafic
items.description: Le poste de péage de Ouaga-route de Pô, à Koubri, a changé d’emplacement. L’Agence de Gestion du Péage (AGP) l’a annoncé dans une note d’information publiée le 25 août 2026. Le nouveau site, situé à l’extérieur de la voie de contournement, est opérationnel depuis ce même mardi, à partir de 8 heures. Désormais, les usagers de la Route nationale 5 doivent s’acquitter de leurs droits de péage à cet endroit. Le poste se trouve à proximité du rond-point menant à Koubri. Pour les automobilistes venant de Koubri, la barrière est placée à l’entrée du rond-point. Ceux qui se rendent à Koubri paieront à la sortie. Selon l’AGP, ce déplacement répond à trois objectifs : renforcer la sécurité des usagers, améliorer la fluidité du trafic et optimiser le recouvrement des recettes. L’agence invite les conducteurs et transporteurs à respecter scrupuleusement la signalisation installée sur place. Elle leur recommande également de préparer la monnaie exacte pour le règlement de leurs tickets, une mesure qui devrait réduire les files d’attente et accélérer le passage. Minute.bf

items.title: Tchamba: Les autorités s’assurent du bon déroulement de l’enregistrement biométrique
items.description: Tchamba, 25 août (ATOP) – Le préfet de Tchamba, Issaka Laguebande, et le maire de la commune Tchamba 1, Hamza Titikpina, ont effectué, le lundi 24 août, une tournée dans plusieurs centres d’enregistrement biométrique de la ville. La tournée s’est déroulée dans plusieurs centres notamment l’EPP Centrale, EPP Watouwa, EPP Larini, au Complexe Jean-Paul II et à l’EPP Iyiwa. L’objectif de cette descente est de constater l’affluence et s’assurer que toutes les dispositions sont prises pour faciliter le recensement des citoyens. Le préfet et le maire ont félicité les agents recenseurs pour la qualité du travail accompli depuis le lancement de l’opération le 21 août. Ils ont invité les agents à faire preuve de patience, d’écoute et de vigilance afin que personne ne soit laissé de côté. Les deux autorités ont insisté sur la prise en charge prioritaire des personnes âgées et des personnes vivant avec un handicap. Elles ont rappelé que l’opération est gratuite et ouverte à tous, sans distinction puis exhorté la population à respecter les directives des agents et à sensibiliser les voisins à venir se faire enrôler. Cette opération se poursuit jusqu’au 21 septembre dans la préfecture de Tchamba. ATOP/SA/MEK/BA

Cameroun : l’UDC se préoccupe de la qualité des résultats attendus du 4e Recensement général de la population
items.description: © DR Au vu des difficultés opérationnelles du dénombrement et des renvois successifs de la fin de l’opération sur le terrain, la présidente de l'Union démocratique du Cameroun interpelle le gouvernement, les partenaires et les populations non encore recensées. La qualité des résultats attendus au terme du 4e Recensement général de la population et de l'habitat couplé au Recensement général de l'agriculture et de l'élevage préoccupe l'Union démocratique du Cameroun (UDC). La présidente du parti, le maire Patricia Tomaino Ndam Njoya exprime sa préoccupation dans une déclaration rendue publique le 23 aout dernier. Motivée par le double renvoi de l'échéance prévue pour la fin du dénombrement ainsi que par les cinq années passées pour publier les résultats du 3eme Recensement effectué en 2005, la femme politique s'interroge. Elle se pose des questions sur l'efficacité et la performance du système. Ainsi que sur la volonté de rendre publique les statistiques fidèles. Lancée le 24 avril 2026, l'opération va s'étendre jusqu'au 15 septembre. A terme, elle aura duré cinq mois. Pourtant, en 2021, la Côte d'Ivoire a recensé près de 30 millions d'habitants en cinq semaines. La préoccupation amène ainsi le leader politique à lancer un appel aux gouvernants et aux partenaires. L'ancienne députée propose de rendre plus inclusive le dénombrement. De s'assurer que les agents recenseurs perçoivent la totalité de leurs indemnités. De déterminer des points fixes où les populations encore non recensées peuvent le faire. Pour la crédibilité de l’opération, Tomaino Ndam Njoya demande aussi au gouvernement d'élaborer un chronogramme d'activités à respecter pour la centralisation des résultats. Aux populations qui traînent le pas, l'UDC appelle à faire un effort. Pour le parti, le recensement n'est pas une campagne politique. C'est une opération visant à actualiser les données de la population, de l'habitat, de l'agriculture, de l'élevage, en vue de favoriser la prise de décisions stratégiques, socio-économiques, politiques et institutionnelles. Après son lancement en avril pour se terminer le 29 mai, le recensement se poursuit à la faveur de deux prolongations. La première décidée par le Premier ministre le 29 mai prévoyait la fin des opérations le 31 juillet. Le même jour, le chef du gouvernement décide d'une nouvelle prorogation fixant la fin du recensement au 15 septembre. Les activités en cours visent à recenser 40% de la population restante. Cet article Cameroun : l'UDC se préoccupe de la qualité des résultats attendus du 4e Recensement général de la population est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Crocodile dans un étang à Adéticopé : les populations appelées à faire preuve de vigilance
items.description: Lomé, 26 août (ATOP) – A travers un communiqué en date du mardi 25 août, le maire de la commune Agoè-Nyivé 6, Songhoi Kézié, informe la population d’Adétikopé qu’un crocodile a été signalé dans un étang situé derrière la Gendarmerie de la localité. Le communiqué précise qu’au regard du risque que représente la présence de cet animal et afin de préserver la sécurité des personnes, l’accès à l’étang ainsi que sa fréquentation sont formellement interdits jusqu’à nouvel ordre. Il est également interdit d’exercer toute activité aux abords immédiats de ce site. Le maire invite la population, notamment les parents, les enfants, les jeunes, les pécheurs et toutes les personnes ayant l’habitude de fréquenter cette zone, à faire preuve de vigilance et à se conformer aux exigences de sécurité. Par ailleurs, l’autorité locale prie toute personne qui viendrait à apercevoir cet animal de ne pas tenter de l’approcher, de le capturer, de le provoquer ou d’intervenir de quelque manière que ce soit. La population est invitée à en informer immédiatement les autorités compétentes car un crocodile reste un animal dangereux et protégé. ATOP/BA/AJA

items.title: Poco Lee’s management breaks silence, denies drink-spiking claims
items.description: The management of Nigerian dancer and singer Poco Lee has broken its silence on the sexual assault case involving the entertainer in the United Kingdom. In a statement issued on Tuesday, August 25, the dancer’s management confirmed that the matter is currently before a UK court and urged the public to allow the legal process to take its course. The team cautioned against treating the allegations as established facts, stressing that Poco Lee has not been convicted of any offence. “Allegations are not evidence of guilt, and no conclusions should be drawn until the matter has been heard and determined through the appropriate legal process,” the statement said. The management also addressed reports circulating online about alleged drink-spiking, clarifying that such claims are not contained in the allegations currently before the court. “We ask the public and media to desist from introducing details that are not part of the actual case, as doing so only fuels misinformation and causes unfair prejudice to all parties involved,” the statement added. Reports of Poco Lee’s arrest in the UK emerged on August 19, with reports linking his detention to a sexual assault allegation. At the time, details surrounding the case, including the identity of the alleged victim and the circumstances of the incident, were not publicly established by British authorities. Amid the reports, a Texas-based Nigerian rapper, Ms Jorji, also made separate allegations against Poco Lee in videos shared online. She claimed that he attempted to sexually assault her and her girlfriend about two years ago during a visit to his home in Dallas. However, her allegations have not been independently verified by a court or law enforcement agency, and no connection has been established between her claims and the ongoing UK case. Poco Lee, whose real name is Iweh Pascal Odinaka, rose to prominence after appearing in Zlatan Ibile’s “Zanku (Legwork)” music video in 2018. He has since become one of Nigeria’s prominent dancers and entertainers, working with several leading artistes, including Davido, Burna Boy, Olamide and Naira Marley. His management said further updates on the case would be communicated through official channels and appealed to the public to exercise patience and restraint while the legal proceedings continue. Vanguard News The post Poco Lee’s management breaks silence, denies drink-spiking claims appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Les Douanes algériennes déploient 14 postes de surveillance aux frontières : leurs missions
items.description: L’Algérie multiplie les mesures pour renforcer les contrôles aux frontières. Après le déploiement d’agents du ministère du Commerce intérieur spécialisés dans la répression des fraudes et le contrôle de la qualité des produits, les Douanes algériennes ajoutent une couche supplémentaire à leur dispositif de surveillance. Une décision datée du 1er juin 2026 portant création des postes de douane de surveillance vient d’entrer en vigueur après sa publication au Journal officiel n°60. Le poste de douane de surveillance est « l'unité structurelle implantée au niveau des frontières terrestres », précise l’article 2 de la décision signée par le directeur général des Douanes algériennes, Abdelhafid Bekhouche. Postes de douane de surveillance aux frontières : voici leurs implantations et leurs missions L’article 3 du même texte a fixé les lieux d’implantation et les missions de ces postes : Assurer une surveillance continue au niveau de la bande frontalière adjacente Apporter le soutien opérationnel aux différentes brigades opérationnelles des douanes, dans la limite de la compétence territoriale Assurer une coordination permanente avec les unités de la gendarmerie nationale compétentes, dans la limite de la compétence territoriale, dans le cadre de la lutte contre toute forme de criminalité transfrontalière Veiller à la sécurité des personnels et des biens au niveau des postes des douanes de surveillance Veiller à la sécurité des marchandises saisies jusqu’à leur remise au receveur des douanes compétent. Au total, 14 postes de surveillance ont été créés par les Douanes algériennes à Tlemcen (05), Naâma (03), Maghnia (02) et Souk Ahras (04). L’article Les Douanes algériennes déploient 14 postes de surveillance aux frontières : leurs missions est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Styrofoam Ban: EPA launches second public awareness campaign in Kumasi
items.description: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) has taken its public awareness campaign on Ghana’s impending ban on polystyrene products to Kumasi, as the country moves closer to the January 2027 implementation of the policy. The Authority is intensifying public education on the rationale behind the ban, the environmental concerns associated with polystyrene products, available alternatives, and what manufacturers, distributors, businesses and consumers must do to prepare for the implementation. The campaign, which is being rolled out through roadshows, market engagements, media interactions and social media outreach, forms part of the EPA’s broader effort to ensure that stakeholders understand the scope of the ban and have adequate time to adjust to the new regime. The Kumasi campaign, being led by the CEO of the authority, Prof Nana Ama Browne Klutse, is the EPA’s second major public awareness exercise targeting the middle belt of the country, following the national campaign launch at Makola in Accra. As part of activities in Kumasi, EPA officials are undertaking a roadshow through some of the city’s principal streets, starting from Anloga Junction and ending at the Kejetia Market. The roadshow is intended to take the campaign directly to traders, consumers and other key stakeholders who use, distribute or have business interests in polystyrene products. At the Kejetia Market, the Authority is expected to hold a mini durbar to engage traders and the public on the environmental and health concerns associated with the use and disposal of Styrofoam products. Officials will also explain the scope of the impending ban, outline alternative products available to businesses and consumers, and respond to concerns from manufacturers, distributors, traders and other stakeholders. The EPA says public education is critical to ensuring a smooth transition ahead of the January 2027 deadline and to minimising disruption to businesses that currently rely heavily on polystyrene packaging. The Kumasi campaign will also feature media engagements aimed at expanding public understanding of the policy and addressing misconceptions surrounding the ban. Meanwhile, the EPA will on Thursday hold a policy engagement dubbed “EPA in Focus”, as part of efforts to highlight key reforms and transformations being introduced under the new Environmental Protection Act. The engagement is expected to provide further insight into the Authority’s evolving mandate, enforcement mechanisms and other institutional reforms being rolled out under the new law. The EPA has repeatedly stressed the need for stronger public participation and stakeholder collaboration as Ghana moves towards more sustainable environmental practices. The ban on polystyrene products is therefore being positioned not only as a regulatory intervention but also as part of a broader effort to reduce plastic pollution and promote environmentally sustainable alternatives. The Authority is urging manufacturers, businesses, traders and consumers to begin preparing ahead of the January 2027 implementation date.

items.title: Presidential campaign council list to be adjusted, not reviewed — Presidency
items.description: The Presidency has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council list for the 2027 election will be adjusted where necessary, but denied that the list has been withdrawn or subjected to a wholesale review. Sunday Dare, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Public Communication, made this known on Wednesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . Dare was responding to reports that the APC had withdrawn the list following controversy over the inclusion and exclusion of some party leaders and other political figures. He said the list remained valid, stressing that the party was yet to constitute all the subcommittees that would make up the campaign structure. “As it is with every other list, there’s a room for subcommittees. Those subcommittees have not been formed, and so many other names will come into that subcommittee,” Dare said. “So that list has not been withdrawn. The APC has issued a statement to that effect yesterday, that list stands. But of course, there will be adjustments. The list is not cast in stone, just like every other list.” The APC had on Tuesday rejected reports that its 2027 presidential campaign council list had been withdrawn. The list, announced over the weekend, named President Tinubu as chairman of the council, with Vice-President Kashim Shettima and APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda as vice chairmen. Former Zamfara State Governor and Senator, Abdul’aziz Yari, was named Director-General, while Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma was designated secretary. Asked whether the list was therefore open to review, Dare avoided the term “review”, describing the expected changes instead as adjustments. “Not a review, just adjustments where necessary,” he said. When pressed on whether his reluctance to use the word “review” meant the list was indeed being reconsidered, the presidential aide maintained that the expected changes did not amount to a comprehensive overhaul. “Review is wholesale, this is not wholesale,” Dare said. He explained that the creation of additional subcommittees would provide room for more party members and political stakeholders to participate in the campaign structure. items.title: Yari’s 2031 Declaration: CSOs, lawyers, others reject APC’s claim to perpetual power
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu, ABUJA Civil society organisations, lawyers and opposition politicians have dismissed the declaration by the Director-General of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari, that the ruling party will remain in power beyond 2031, saying political power belongs to the electorate and not any political party. Read Also: Highways of horror: Motorists wail, spend 4 days on Benin-Asaba road The groups warned that while the APC was entitled to aspire to retain power, predicting electoral victories years ahead could create a dangerous impression of political entitlement, undermine confidence in elections and discourage citizens from participating in the democratic process. They spoke against the backdrop of Yari’s recent declaration that the APC would continue governing Nigeria beyond 2031. Executive Director of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre, CISLAC, Auwal Rafsanjani, described Yari’s position as “an expression of partisan optimism”, insisting that it must not be presented as though future electoral outcomes had already been determined. Rafsanjani said: “The Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre, CISLAC, considers the declaration by the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari, that the APC will continue to govern Nigeria beyond 2031 as an expression of partisan optimism, but one that must not be presented as if Nigeria’s future electoral outcomes have already been decided and determined. “In a democracy, however, no political party has a permanent entitlement to power. The authority to determine who governs Nigeria in 2027, 2031 or any subsequent election belongs exclusively to Nigerian voters through credible, competitive, free and fair elections.” The CISLAC boss warned that such utterances could undermine Nigerians’ confidence in the electoral process, describing it as careless to make statements suggesting predetermined electoral victories ahead of the 2027 general elections. Osun poll, a reality check Rafsanjani urged the APC and other political parties not to overlook the lessons of the recent Osun State governorship election, saying the outcome demonstrated that Nigerian voters could not be taken for granted. “The recent Osun State governorship election provides an important reality check for every political party, including the APC,” he said. According to him, “This election demonstrates clearly that Nigerian voters cannot simply be taken for granted. “Even a governing party with substantial political structures, influential personalities and access to significant campaign machinery can be defeated where voters decide otherwise. “Therefore, the Osun election does not support the assumption that any political party can confidently predict that it will remain in power until or beyond 2031. “Rather, it demonstrates that electoral power ultimately rests with citizens when their votes are allowed to count.” He said political parties should focus less on declarations of prolonged rule and more on addressing the problems confronting Nigerians. “Instead of political leaders making declarations about ruling Nigeria for another several years, CISLAC believes attention should be directed towards the urgent concerns confronting ordinary Nigerians. “Nigerians will judge political parties and candidates based on their ability to address insecurity, unemployment, poverty, inflation and the cost of living, corruption, deteriorating public services and citizens’ confidence in governance institutions.” Rafsanjani added that the governing party should allow its performance to determine whether Nigerians would renew its mandate. “Political dominance should not be achieved through incumbency advantage, manipulation of electoral institutions, intimidation of opposition parties, vote-buying, abuse of state resources or weakening of democratic institutions. It should come only through the freely expressed mandate of citizens. “CISLAC urges not only the APC but every political party participating in the 2027 elections to understand that Nigeria belongs to its citizens, not to any particular party.” He advised political parties to base their campaigns on programmes, ideas and records rather than predictions of victory. “Campaigns should therefore focus on ideas, programmes, track records and solutions, rather than declarations suggesting predetermined electoral victories,” he said. The CISLAC director also charged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, security agencies and other state institutions to remain neutral. “The responsibility of INEC, security agencies and other state institutions is equally important. They must remain politically neutral and ensure that no political party—whether governing or opposition—is given an unfair advantage.” He stressed that Yari and the APC had the right to seek continued control of government, but could not claim ownership of the future. “Senator Yari and the APC are entitled to aspire to remain in government beyond 2031, just as opposition parties are entitled to aspire to replace them. But aspiration must never be confused with entitlement. “Ultimately, 2031 belongs neither to APC nor to any opposition party. It belongs to the Nigerian people. The ballot, not political declarations, must determine who governs Nigeria.” ‘Yari disregards electorate’ Human rights lawyer, Idris Faro, also faulted Yari’s declaration, saying electoral victory was determined by voters and not pronouncements by politicians. “Electoral victory is ordinarily determined by the programmes and policies implemented by a political party. It is not determined by an unguarded statement of a politician. “To assert that your party will rule beyond 2031 shows that you have no regard for the role and power of the electorate,” Faro stated. He said a politician confident in his party’s performance should point to achievements and allow voters to make the final judgment. “A careful politician would state that with the number of transport infrastructure done, economic reforms introduced which have stabilised the economy, and constitutional amendments passed, he believes his party will win future elections.” Faro added: “Historical evidence runs contrary to that reckless assertion. Your hope ought to be based on the appreciation of your projects and scores given by the voters.” Nigerians’ll decide — ActionAid Country Director, ActionAid Nigeria, Dr Andrew Mamedu, said no government or political party could guarantee victory in 2027 or any subsequent election because the ultimate power rested with Nigerians. “For us in civil society, we insist that there should be free, fair and credible elections so that the votes of the people, the voice of the people is what matters, what counts at the end of the day,” Mamedu said. “So a particular administration cannot, nobody can say for certain that they will win this election, win the next election. “From what Senator Yari has said, it means that they will win this coming election and win the next one, but that’s not for him to say, that’s not for him to decide. “It is left for the people of Nigeria to decide, it’s left for the citizens of Nigeria and that majority of the citizens to decide. So people should come out and cast their vote.” Mamedu, however, said Yari’s statement could also be interpreted as a challenge to the APC to improve its performance. “On the other hand, it could mean that APC, of course, would need to sit up from what they are doing right now. “There are clear indications that people are still feeling the hardship, people are still feeling, are still looking for more good governance from all across, from both federal and states, across board.” According to him, the ruling party could retain power if it performed better and implemented policies that improved citizens’ welfare. “So it could mean that APC, Senator Yari, is saying that the APC is going to sit up and do better, that’s another way to interpret it, that if they do better, if they implement pro-poor policies, policies that concern the people, positively affect the people, then of course people will vote them in and vote them back.” He, however, warned against any interpretation suggesting that the APC intended to retain power through illegitimate means. “Or it could also mean that they are thinking that they will come in and they would do that by all means possible. Could that also mean that they would want to get into power by all means possible, including doing things that are illegitimate or illegal? ‘Don’t be frightened’ Mamedu said Yari was speaking as a politician and urged Nigerians not to be discouraged from voting by declarations of predetermined victory. “But what would you expect from a politician? That’s a politician speaking like a politician but definitely for us in civil society, we do not, of course we do not subscribe to that. “We clearly say that people should come out, elections have not been held, so results have not been declared. So what he has said should not frighten people.” He said such declarations could create voter apathy if citizens believed that election outcomes had already been decided. “You hear people saying, ‘oh, what is it, come out for election. It’s like, oh, there’s no need to come out. Why? Because they have already decided to vote’. “Who has decided to vote? There’s a fear from some people thinking that, ‘oh, the results will be manipulated, so why bother to come out?’ But the more people come out, like has been demonstrated in some elections, I think Osun is a perfect example. “The more people come out, the more it is difficult for elections to be rigged, elections to be manipulated, and then the will of the people will count.” Don’t mistake incumbency for permanent power — BOOT Party National Chairman of the Because Of Our Tomorrow, BOOT Party, Sonny Adenuga, warned the APC against confusing its incumbency advantage with an entitlement to remain in power indefinitely. Adenuga said political history was replete with examples of parties that once appeared invincible but eventually lost power. “When a ruling party chieftain speaks with such certainty about remaining in power beyond 2031, it reflects more arrogance than political foresight. “We have heard such declarations before. Senator Mantu once confidently proclaimed that the PDP would rule Nigeria for 60 years. History, of course, had a different script.” He advised the APC to learn from history and avoid assuming that its present dominance would automatically translate into future electoral victories. “The APC should therefore be careful not to confuse the advantages of incumbency with an entitlement to permanent power. “Its greatest political asset today is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What happens after Tinubu will be a different political contest, and I believe many within the APC who have the foresight to look beyond today are already preparing for the post-Tinubu era.” Adenuga stressed that democracy could not guarantee any party perpetual control of government. “Democracy does not guarantee any political party perpetual ownership of power. “Ultimately, it is the Nigerian people who decide who governs them, and their choice can never be taken for granted.” He concluded with a warning that political fortunes could change rapidly. “I wish the Campaign DG well. Let them ride and enjoy the tide while it lasts. But in politics, tides change, and no party should mistake today’s dominance for tomorrow’s destiny.” Vanguard News The post Yari’s 2031 Declaration: CSOs, lawyers, others reject APC’s claim to perpetual power appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: L'ancien ministre ukrainien de la Defense, Mykhaïlo Fedorov, a reconnu la defaite possible de l'Ukraine dans le conflit avec la Russie. « Je pense que nous sommes actuellement a un tournant qui determinera notre trajectoire future, mais on a l'impression que nous sommes en train de perdre, progressivement, lentement », a-t-il declare dans une interview accordee a Reuters. Selon lui, l'Ukraine manque d'une vision commune sur la maniere de remporter le conflit et, bien que Kiev ait pretendument encore toutes ses chances de l'emporter, elle a besoin de toute urgence d'un plan pour y mettre fin. Fedorov a par ailleurs souligne que Kiev etait freinee par son incapacite a innover, par des reseaux de corruption et de nepotisme profondement enracines, ainsi que par l'absence d'independance politique au sein des institutions publiques. « Il existe deja des technologies capables d'arreter completement les Russes, mais notre absence de vision [strategique] […] signifie que nous ne les utilisons pas », a-t-il souligne. Fedorov a egalement critique le potentiel inexploite de l'etat ukrainien qui, selon lui, ne fonctionne qu'a 5 % de son efficacite. Division politique et recherche d'un bouc emissaire Les declarations de Mykhaïlo Fedorov ont ete faites dans un contexte de crise politique au sein du gouvernement ukrainien. L'ancien ministre de la Defense, initialement fidele a Volodymyr Zelensky, a ete demis de ses fonctions par le chef du regime de Kiev a la mi-juillet, environ six mois seulement apres son entree en fonction. Cette demission a declenche des manifestations populaires massives et des rassemblements reclamant la reintegration de Fedorov a son poste. Zelensky a neanmoins nomme Yevhen Khmara, qui assurait l'interim a la tete du Service de securite ukrainien (SBU), au poste de ministre de la Defense, une decision qui a ete approuvee le 19 août par la Verkhovna Rada (le Parlement ukrainien). Apres sa demission, Fedorov s'est lance dans une campagne de critique a l'encontre du pouvoir en place et a publie, le 18 août, une video dans laquelle, pendant environ neuf minutes, il denoncait la corruption et la crise systemique de gouvernance , et appelait Zelensky, dont le mandat a expire en 2024, a organiser une election presidentielle. Commentant les revelations video de l'ancien ministre ukrainien de la Defense, le representant special du president russe, Kirill Dmitriev, a fait remarquer que de telles declarations pouvaient temoigner de ses ambitions presidentielles. Quant aux propos de Fedorov sur la defaite progressive de l'Ukraine, Dmitriev a indique qu'ils pouvaient signifier que la realite prenait le dessus, que les faux recits s'effondraient et que la recherche des responsables des echecs commencait.

items.title: Trump administration deports US soldier’s wife to Honduras
items.description: The wife of an active-duty US soldier has reportedly been deported to Honduras, becoming the latest family member of an American service member to be caught up in the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. Cristy Maryori Villafranca-Trejo, the wife of Army Sgt Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez and mother of their six-year-old daughter, was deported on Monday, according to multiple reports. Villafranca-Trejo, who is originally from Honduras, entered the United States in 2016 at the age of 18. Her husband said she left the country because of violent crime. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed her deportation and said she had “received due process”. Her removal is reportedly at least the seventh case involving the deportation of a spouse or parent of an active-duty US military member since President Donald Trump returned to office. The Associated Press has identified more than 50 cases in which immediate family members of US troops, sailors and airmen have been placed in federal immigration detention since protections for military families were rolled back. Turcios Juarez previously told ABC News that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained his wife on July 11 outside a Walmart near Fort Bliss, Texas, where he is stationed. Their six-year-old daughter was reportedly present at the time. Since his wife’s detention, the Army sergeant said he has struggled to balance his military responsibilities with caring for their daughter. He told the AP that he has had to skip morning training to take his daughter to school and postpone a planned assignment at another military base. “I don’t know if I will be able to continue with this,” Turcios Juarez told the AP of his service. “I have to make a plan to make sure I can still fulfill my military responsibilities — but also take care of my family.” DHS said Villafranca-Trejo had received a final order of removal from an immigration judge in 2017 after she failed to appear at a hearing. However, her husband said she never received notice of the hearing and was unaware that she had been ordered to leave the country until 2022, when the couple sought to apply for her green card after getting married. Turcios Juarez, who is also originally from Honduras, became a US citizen in 2024 after joining the Army in 2022. Villafranca-Trejo had also been waiting for about a year for a decision on her application for military parole-in-place, a programme that can allow certain immediate family members of US military personnel to remain in the country while pursuing lawful permanent residence. “We were following the rules, we did everything we could on our side to fix this problem,” Turcios Juarez told the AP. The case comes amid growing concern over the impact of the administration’s immigration enforcement measures on US military families. items.title: 'Heads must roll': Politicians, journalists demand accountability as Pims fire claims lives of 14 infants
items.description: Fourteen infants were killed on Wednesday morning in a fire at the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), Islamabad’s premier public hospital. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said that the incident occurred at 6:45am due to a “blast in the air conditioner” inside the ward and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif swiftly removed the federal health secretary as an inquiry was launched. However, the incident sparked outrage among politicians and journalists, who demanded accountability and termed it the outcome of “criminal negligence”. PPP leader Senator Sherry Rehman called the incident “beyond shocking” and held that it was a “deep stain of shame on the entire ministry and the rot within”. “This is where citizens are sent to heal in the federal capital?” Rehman asked as she called for justice for the lives lost. Awaam Pakistan leader and former finance minister Miftah Ismail called for a “full investigation” into the incident. “This is beyond tragic. This is criminal negligence. There should be full investigation and accountability and heads must roll,” he said. Journalist Fahd Husain said that the incident was “not just a tragedy but a crime committed by all those who are entrusted with running the hospital and their bosses”. He held that it was a “by-product of atrocious governance, criminal apathy and inefficient government machinery that is rotten to the core”. Assailing the authorities, Husain said that statements from leaders expressing “ afsos ” (grief) over the incident were nothing but “salt [in the] the wounds by these very people”. Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan leader and former Senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar said PM Shehbaz taking notice of the fire was “simply not enough” as the incident was the result of “criminal negligence”. “Fourteen infants losing their lives in an incident which could have been prevented by better management and oversight, can’t be shrugged off,” Khokhar said. Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief and leader of the opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas expressed sorrow at the deaths of the infants, saying that the incident must not be “dismissed as a mere accident and ignored”. “This tragedy raises doubts over the security arrangements, administrative supervision and government priorities in hospitals,” he said. Calling the incident a “failure on the part of the system of governance,” he called for an “immediate, transparent, impartial and high-level” investigation and for the hospital administration, along with relevant authorities, to be held accountable. He also called for an investigation into the alleged late arrival of rescue teams and the immediate resignation of the health minister. PPP lawmaker Sharmila Faruqui also called on the health minister to tender his resignation immediately. “If there is any such thing left as political and moral responsibility in this country, then Health Minister Mustafa Kamal should immediately tender his resignation,” she said. Referring to the federal health secretary’s dismissal, she maintained that he was being used “as a scapegoat to absolve the health minister of his responsibility”, adding that the hospitals in Islamabad were under Kamal’s “direct responsibility”. “When he cannot ensure basic management, oversight, and patient safety in the hospitals under his administration, then what justification remains for running the health ministry?” National Democratic Movement leader Bushra Gohar called for the hospital administration to be held accountable and for the health minister to accept responsibility and resign. “Compensation to grieving families cannot be used to silence them or substitute for justice. The families deserve accountability, transparency and justice not hush money,” she wrote. Dawn journalist Baqir Sajjad Syed said the children “were entrusted to the hospital for care and protection, not to lose their lives to a preventable tragedy”. He noted that the lack of safety measures and regulatory oversight made the loss “even more painful”. “Who can now remedy the agony of parents who lost their newborns?” he asked. “This is too tragic. Very painful,” said former Sindh governor Mohammad Zubair. “This government can’t even manage a hospital in Islamabad,” he said. Journalist Hasnaat Malik referred to a recent statement by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, saying: “We have been told that good governance would come through establishing small units. “But why there is no ‘good governance’ in Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). Pims tragedy is the classic example of criminal negligence, bad governance and maladministration,” he said. “Fourteen infants have been burnt to death in a fire in Islamabad’s largest public sector hospital, in Pakistan’s capital and its premier showcase of modern urban life. Let that sink in,” said journalist Iftikhar Firdous. “Apathy cannot be repackaged as endurance and sold to the public after every national tragedy. Stop romanticising the suffering of your own people and fix the system,” he said. Journalist Yusra Askari said that no words, no visits and no compensation would give the bereaved families patience. “Those responsible for mammoth negligence have to be held accountable,” she said. Journalist Fereeha Idrees criticised the government for its failure to protect babies “in the most central hospital in the federal territory”. Objecting to statements issued by the authorities, she said: “With due respect, just by writing ‘strict’ in every word doesn’t entail strict action. What strict action has the PM taken, please? Only secretary health removed and [an] emergency meeting called by [the] PM. Is this strict action?” She asserted that the government had failed to protect the lives of the children. Header image: An ambulance transporting the remains of a child drives past police following a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP
